item.title: RAMP: Recurrent Adaptive Mixed Precision for Efficient Prefill in Recurrent-Depth Language Models
item.description: RAMP replaces uniform-precision recurrent prefill with a schedule that runs early recurrent steps in low-precision weight-and-activation arithmetic and restores full precision for terminal steps, exploiting the finding that early quantization errors are attenuated by later refinement. The cost is implementation complexity in the recurrent inference loop and the need for weight-and-activation quantization kernels, with quality risk if the error-attenuation property does not hold for a given model. It can fail on non-recurrent architectures, on workloads dominated by decode rather than prefill, and beyond the 4K context lengths actually validated. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: KV-Repurpose: A Testbed for Evaluating Non-Prefix KV-Cache Reuse
item.description: Replaces exact-prefix KV-cache reuse with segment-wise reuse, allowing cached document blocks to be reused across different system prompts and conversation histories in a vLLM-based serving stack. Costs include adopting and maintaining a custom scheduling, prompt-construction, and capacity-management layer on top of vLLM, plus engineering effort to segment workloads correctly. Naive segment reuse largely preserves quality on single-document QA and summarization, but the paper reports clear degradation in cross-document reasoning, and the reported gains are demonstrated only under a specific Zipfian RAG workload, so real traffic may benefit far less. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: TPCS: A Cycle-Level Simulation Paradigm with Native Execution Semantics for RTL Modeling and Generation
item.description: TPCS replaces event-driven RTL simulation (e.g., Verilator) with a transaction-based intermediate abstraction that uses host CPU control flow to prune inactive logic while remaining translatable to synthesizable RTL. Its cost is adoption of a new modeling framework and toolchain rather than compute or memory, since simulation runs on a host CPU. It can fail if the evaluated traces do not represent the reader's designs, if automatic RTL generation misses corner cases requiring explicit event semantics, or if ecosystem immaturity limits integration with existing verification flows. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Scaling Agentic Data for Long-Horizon Terminal Intelligence
item.description: The method replaces manually authored or naively synthesized agent training environments with a fully automated engine that reconstructs environments to preserve exploration, implementation, and verification work, then progressively expands tasks into long-horizon trajectories for supervised fine-tuning. Adopting it costs the compute to run the synthesis engine, independent execution verification, and full SFT of a 27B model, which exceeds a single 24 GB GPU and a limited cloud budget. It can fail if environment reconstruction silently reintroduces shortcuts the independent-execution check misses, and the reported gains may not transfer to a smaller model that fits the reader's infrastructure. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: RoleWorld: Knowledge Transfer in World Modeling with Functional Role Abstractions
item.description: It replaces environment-specific symbolic rules or programs with reusable functional role prototypes plus environment-specific parameter estimates, keeping transition rules fixed and refining role assignments online without LLM parameter updates. Cost is a teacher-LLM extraction phase per source environment, additional actor-LLM calls for skill-guided decision making and uncertainty-driven hypothesis testing, plus the engineering burden of maintaining executable rules, role assignments, and parameter estimators. It can fail when the teacher extracts incorrect or non-transferable role abstractions, when online parameter estimation converges too slowly or wrongly, or when the target environment's dynamics do not actually share the assumed interaction structure. 1 independent implementation, 338 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: test.

item.title: JANUS: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models
item.description: JANUS replaces reactive trial-and-error Generate-Execute-Feedback loops in autonomous research agents with a Predict-Verify-Evolve loop in which a co-evolving world model scores, prunes, and refines candidate branches before costly executions. The cost is maintaining an evolving candidate graph, a forecasting world model, hierarchical skill stores, and their coordination protocols, which adds orchestration complexity and extra model calls per iteration. Failure modes include miscalibrated world-model forecasts pruning valuable branches early, error compounding as skills and predictions co-evolve over long horizons, and limited transferability of gains demonstrated primarily on one benchmark. 3 independent implementations, 353 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: S$^3$R: Fast and Faithful RL Rollouts via Self-Sparse Speculative Decoding
item.description: The method replaces direct sparse-attention sampling (or plain autoregressive decoding) in RLVR rollout generation with sparse-attention drafting followed by full-attention verification and exact speculative sampling, so response groups remain faithful to the dense-policy distribution. It costs a modified inference stack: shared-parameter drafting plus verification passes, retention of the complete historical KV cache for verification, and a KV-aware scheduler to avoid offloading and restoration thrashing. It can fail because the speedup depends on draft acceptance rates and aggressive sparse budgets, requires rollout-scale infrastructure and custom scheduling unavailable on a single 24 GB GPU, and the reported gains are limited to long-context mathematical RLVR on Qwen3. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: How Much Computation Does Every Forecast Need? Structured Block Skipping in Two Time-Series Foundation Models
item.description: The method replaces full-depth forward passes in pretrained time-series foundation models with statically masked Transformer blocks, where whole blocks are bypassed using masks selected on calibration windows. It costs a calibration procedure per deployment setting and carries quality risk: aggressive skipping substantially degrades Traffic and Weather, and the measured latency gain is only 11-13% at the moderate sparsity that preserves accuracy. What can fail is generalization: dataset-specific masks transfer inconsistently, per-window optimal masks differ so no static mask captures the oracle opportunity, and Chronos representations do not support reliable routing to unseen domains. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Monarch-MoE: Structured Experts for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
item.description: Monarch-MoE replaces the dense low-rank factors in multi-expert LoRA adapters with block-diagonal factors joined by a fixed permutation, so each block-pair update touches only one output block and forgetting is reduced in multimodal continual instruction tuning. The cost is a custom implementation with batched computation, fused forward operators, and a specialized backward pass, plus method-dependent trade-offs in final-task performance; parameter savings are a side benefit rather than guaranteed speedups outside the evaluated setup. It can fail if the reader's workload is not continual multimodal instruction tuning of a ~7B VLM, since gains are validated only on MLLM-DCL and UCIT with LLaVA-1.5-7B, and the fixed permutation may underperform dense factors on other task sequences. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Understanding and Mitigating Cross-Session Attacks via Persistent Artifacts in Agent Skill Composition
item.description: It replaces unguarded cross-session skill execution, in which persistent artifacts are consumed without provenance context, with a runtime layer that restores artifact provenance and adds a pre-execution advisory review while leaving the final decision to the agent. The cost is additional engineering to record and propagate artifact provenance, extra review latency and prompt/context tokens per skill invocation, and possible advisory false positives that can block or alter legitimate flows. It can fail because the final execution choice remains with the agent, roughly one in ten attacks still succeeds in the reported setting, and provenance can be incomplete across sessions, tools, or artifact types outside the evaluated benchmark. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Forgetting is Not Always Bad: A Neuro-Inspired Memory Repair Mechanism for Poisoned LLM Agents
item.description: DREAM replaces external memory-isolation or continuous online-auditing modules for defending LLM agents against memory poisoning with an agent-intrinsic, training-free three-stage pipeline (perturbation-induced reactivation, anomaly diagnosis, selective memory suppression and reinforcement). It requires no model training and fits a single-GPU or API-based stack, but adds per-step inference overhead for reactivation and diagnosis, and its cost depends on how often repair passes must run. It can fail through false positives that suppress benign memories, degraded robustness against adaptive attackers not covered in the evaluation, and the need to revalidate detection thresholds for each memory backend and task distribution. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Agent4Spec: An LLM-based Agentic System to Optimize API Specifications through Automated Validation and Market Analysis
item.description: Agent4Spec replaces manual, one-time authoring and maintenance of OpenAPI specifications with a two-pipeline multi-agent system that self-corrects syntax errors and proposes market-driven endpoint additions. It costs multiple coordinated LLM calls per specification, which is feasible on third-party APIs with no local GPU requirement, but adds orchestration complexity and per-document token spend compared with a single lint-and-review pass. It can fail when the validation loop accepts plausible but semantically wrong corrections, and the market-analysis pipeline can generate endpoint suggestions based on unreliable competitive research that engineers must still review, since roughly half of suggestions were not adopted. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Beyond the Final Embedding: Retrieving Memories from Token-Level Evidence
item.description: The method replaces single-vector query-memory similarity with sparse token-level matching over the contextual token representations already produced by the embedding model, aggregated and combined with whole-memory similarity, optionally refined by a low-rank query adapter trained while the encoder and stored representations stay fixed. The training-free variant costs only token-level index storage and per-query matching latency, but storing token representations for all memories is substantially larger than one vector per memory, and the adapter variant adds a supervised training step with labeled data. It can fail when query-token matches fire on irrelevant memories (raising false positives), when token index size or scoring latency exceeds the memory retrieval budget, and when gains on the eight reported benchmarks do not transfer to the reader's memory distribution. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: test.

item.title: PRIME: Pre-Retrieval Index Modeling Enhancement for Structured Document Retrieval-Real
item.description: PRIME replaces plain chunk-based corpus indexing with an index-side pipeline: LLM-driven semantic restructuring of documents plus deterministic metadata extraction and hierarchical section retrieval. It costs LLM calls at index time, added indexing complexity, and a quality-fidelity trade-off from restructuring, though it reduces embedding compute and vector count by large factors. It can degrade retrieval in certain corpus regimes (three qualitative failure/success regimes are reported), and its gains are neutralized when a strong reranker is used downstream. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Masked Diffusion Language Agents for Tool-Integrated Chemical Reasoning
item.description: It replaces autoregressive left-to-right generation in tool-using agents with iterative masked-diffusion denoising over interleaved reasoning and tool-call trajectories, so tool decisions are conditioned on full-trajectory bidirectional context rather than only the past. The cost is a non-standard masked-diffusion model plus a two-stage post-training pipeline (agentic supervised fine-tuning and variance-reduced preference optimization), iterative multi-step denoising at inference, and tooling for diffusion-LM serving that is far less mature than the autoregressive stack. It can fail because the reported gains hold only on the authors' chemistry benchmark under matched budgets and may not transfer to other domains, and arbitrary-order decoding offers little benefit on strictly sequential tasks while the absence of optimized KV-cache and batching support can erode the quality advantage in latency and serving complexity. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: watch.
